title: Long Way Round
summary: London to New York the long way: east across Europe, the Kazakh and Mongolian steppe, Siberia and the Road of Bones to Magadan, then across Alaska, Canada and the US. About 30,000 km in under four months, filmed as a TV series that inspired a generation of adventure riders.
approximate: Countries, key places and dates follow public accounts; the exact roads between them are approximate.

stops.name: London
stops.text: The start, from their workshop in west London: two heavily loaded BMWs, a support crew of two 4x4s, and 19,000 miles ahead.

stops.name: Calais
stops.text: Through the Channel Tunnel by train, one of the few stretches of the trip not ridden.

photo.credit: Billy69150 (voir les conditions d'utilisation / see licensing below)

stops.name: Brussels
stops.text: Belgium and Germany pass in a blur of motorway: the easy part, before the real borders begin.

stops.name: Prague
stops.text: A night in Prague. The Czech exit later cost them a "fine" for a missing stamp in the bikes' carnet, a first taste of border paperwork.

stops.name: Kutná Hora
stops.text: The Church of Bones at Sedlec: a chapel decorated with the bones of tens of thousands of people. A strange, unforgettable stop.

stops.name: Into Ukraine
stops.text: Across Slovakia and into Ukraine, where roads, signs and border queues change character.

stops.name: Kyiv
stops.text: East across the wide Ukrainian plains towards Russia.

stops.name: Volgograd
stops.text: The old Stalingrad on the Volga, watched over by the giant Motherland Calls statue. Russian visas had been one of the hardest parts of planning.

stops.name: Atyrau
stops.text: Into Kazakhstan where the Ural river meets the Caspian: the start of thousands of kilometres of steppe, wild camping and broken roads.

stops.name: Almaty
stops.text: Kazakhstan's green southern city under the Tian Shan mountains, a rest after the long empty steppe.

stops.name: Semey
stops.text: North through eastern Kazakhstan towards the Russian Altai.

stops.name: Barnaul
stops.text: Back into Russia, heading for the Altai mountains and the Mongolian border.

stops.name: Ölgii
stops.text: Mongolia: no tarmac, few signs, rivers to ford and endless open land. Some of the hardest and most loved days of the trip.

stops.name: Khovd
stops.text: Sandy tracks and river crossings across western Mongolia. The support truck rolled here; the bikes took a beating too.

stops.name: Ulaanbaatar
stops.text: Mongolia's capital after weeks of steppe and nights in gers with nomad families.

stops.name: Ulan-Ude
stops.text: Back into Siberia, near Lake Baikal.

stops.name: Chita
stops.text: East along the Trans-Siberian corridor to where the road ran out.

stops.name: Tynda
stops.text: The Zilov Gap had no road at all, so bikes and riders took the train for about 930 km.

stops.name: Yakutsk
stops.text: The world's coldest big city, and the start of the Kolyma Highway east to the Pacific.

stops.name: Road of Bones
stops.text: The Road of Bones, built by Gulag prisoners. In summer melt the rivers were deep and fast, and some crossings needed a passing truck to carry the bikes.

stops.name: Magadan
stops.text: The end of the road on the Sea of Okhotsk, with the Mask of Sorrow memorial to the Gulag prisoners. Asia done.

stops.name: Anchorage
stops.text: A 4,000 km flight across the Bering Sea from Magadan to Alaska, then back on the bikes.

photo.credit: Frank K. from Anchorage, Alaska, USA

stops.name: Whitehorse
stops.text: Down the Alaska Highway into Canada's Yukon: big forests, bears, and smooth roads after Siberia.

stops.name: Calgary
stops.text: Out of the Rockies and onto the Canadian prairies.

stops.name: Mount Rushmore
stops.text: Across the border into the US and to the presidents carved into the Black Hills.

stops.name: Chicago
stops.text: The last long days east across the Midwest.

photo.credit: File:Chicago River ferry.jpg: John Picken derivative work: Georgfotoart

stops.name: New York
stops.text: Arrival on schedule, escorted into the city by a crowd of bikers. London to New York, the long way round.
